headword: {終|お}わりよければすべてよし
reading: おわりよければすべてよし

definitions.explanation: A proverb meaning that as long as the final outcome is good, any difficulties or problems along the way can be forgiven or forgotten.

examples.japanese: {終|お}わりよければすべてよしだ。
⟦{途中|とちゅう}→途中：01684_tochuu⟧いろいろ⟦あった→ある：00006_aru⟧⟦けど→けど：09477_kedo⟧、{終|お}わりよければすべてよしだ⟦よ→よ：09475_yo⟧。
examples.english: There were various things along the way, but all's well that ends well.

examples.japanese: ⟦{失敗|しっぱい}→失敗：01636_shippai⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦あった→ある：00006_aru⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{最後|さいご}→最後：01413_saigo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{成功|せいこう}した→成功する：21445_seikousuru⟧。{終|お}わりよければすべてよし⟦という→という：09577_toiu⟧ことだ。
examples.english: There were failures, but it succeeded in the end. All's well that ends well, as they say.

notes:
A well-known Japanese proverb equivalent to the English "all's well that ends well." The structure breaks down as: ⟦{終|お}わり→終わり：01361_owari⟧ (ending) + ⟦よければ→いい：00118_ii⟧ (if good) + すべて (everything) + ⟦よし→よし：10741_yoshi⟧ (is good).

USAGE:
Used to console or encourage after a difficult process that ultimately turned out well. Often said with a sense of relief when looking back on hardships. Can also be used to brush off complaints about methods when the final result is satisfactory.
